reason: Start with the kidney filter to follow how blood becomes filtrate, one of the chapter's goals.
expectation: I expect the nephron to filter some fluid and dissolved substances from the blood, while retaining blood cells.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the ureters would advance the organ assembly, but I want to follow filtration first.

effect: The filter passes fluid and small dissolved substances into the tubule while retaining cells and most proteins, so the next step is to follow recovery.
reaction: The cross-section makes the filter's selectivity clear.
reason: Add the tubule transporters to see how useful substances are reclaimed.
expectation: I expect some dissolved substances to move from the tubule back toward the blood; I am unsure which ones will be shown.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would advance the urinary organ assembly, but I want to follow the filtrate first.

effect: The tubule recovers glucose and other useful substances, so I can now follow water recovery.
reaction: The distinction between filtering glucose and reclaiming it is useful.
reason: Continue following the filtered sample through water recovery.
expectation: I expect some water to move from the tubule back toward the blood, leaving a more concentrated remaining fluid.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the ureters would advance the organ assembly, but I want to finish following the sample first.

effect: Water returns to the blood while wastes remain in the tubule; the remaining sample can now be followed into urinary drainage.
reaction: The picture makes the contrast between water recovery and retained wastes clear.
reason: Continue following the sample toward urine before assembling the organs.
expectation: I expect the remaining fluid to pass into the urinary drainage route as urine.

effect: The remaining fluid reaches the bladder as urine, completing the filtering and recovery goal. The urinary organs still need connecting to the body.
reaction: The drainage picture completes the sample's route clearly.
reason: Attach the ureters to start assembling the urinary organs.
expectation: I expect the ureters to connect to the kidneys, leaving the bladder to be fitted.

alternatives.reason: The bladder can also be fitted, but the ureters follow the route from kidneys toward the bladder.

effect: The ureters are fitted to the kidney pair; the bladder is the remaining organ fitting.
reaction: The result confirms the fitting, though the picture description adds little about the connection.
reason: Fit the bladder to continue assembling the urinary organs; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the bladder to join the kidney and ureter assembly, ready for connection to the body.

effect: The bladder is fitted, completing the kidney-to-bladder assembly; it can now be connected to the body.
reaction: The explanation clearly traces urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
reason: Connect the assembled urinary organs to the body; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the kidneys and urinary drainage organs to join the body and its circulation, completing the remaining goal.

effect: The urinary organs are connected to the body's circulation, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The final picture plan brings the filtration and drainage routes together, though briefly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Recovering glucose after filtration was most worthwhile: it clarified that useful substances can enter the filtrate and then return to blood.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters added little in its picture description; the subsequent bladder fitting explained the route more clearly.

surprise.text: The distinction between glucose passing through the filter and almost all of it normally being recovered was the most useful change in my understanding.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the ureter fitting was a predictable assembly step rather than a meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would be willing to continue: tracing filtration and recovery made the constructions useful, although the organ fittings were less engaging.
